title: Profile pack: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (IQ3_S GSQ-RCO) on a patched Strata build, one desktop PC - generator test run
intro: **What this is.** How a 512-expert MoE model runs on one desktop PC with 24 GB of VRAM over two GPUs and 96 GB of RAM: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (published as a preview of the Qwen4 architecture) as the ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ3_S GGUF, on the Strata engine (upstream v0.2.8) plus the owner's patch series (build label **P028x**), since 2026-11-09 20:06 on the **fetch build**, which adds upstream's STRATA_ADAPT_FETCH and runs it beside the helper GPU; served locally on 127.0.0.1. All routed experts sit in pinned RAM (46.8 GiB); the main GPU caches 18.7 % of them and a helper GPU another 13.4 %. Because routing is skewed, and because the fetch build keeps often-routed experts that it had to read over PCIe in the main GPU's cache, those caches serve about 85 % of the routed expert work during decode on the 11-09 screen (80 % on the same screen before the fetch patch; section 5). Everything is lossless by the owner's rule: no switch that changes outputs beyond rounding is served. **Older measurements:** where the current build was not measured, the pack keeps figures from the P028x engine before the fetch patch (2026-11-09 or earlier) and says so where they appear: the per-window time split of section 8 (measured 11-05; it is also the source of the 'decode window' row in the table below, so that row describes the P028x engine before the fetch patch), the ten-day served-log figures, the 3-pass pp16k / pp64k fixtures (the current build has one pass of each) and the reference sets P, P-screen and PU. This file is the test run of a generator that will write the same pack for Qwen4 on its release day; section 10 lists what today's files only approximate.

hardware.main_gpu: NVIDIA RTX 5080 16 GB, PCIe Gen5 x16 (runs the model; no display attached)
hardware.helper_gpu: NVIDIA RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB on a chipset PCIe Gen4 x4 link (a second expert cache only)
hardware.ram: 96 GB DDR5-6000 (about 77 GB/s measured); the desktop display runs on the CPU's integrated graphics
hardware.storage: Samsung 9100 PRO 2 TB NVMe (Gen5 x4), holds the model files

engine_label: P028x on the fetch build = upstream Strata v0.2.8 + the owner's patch series (P028x, served since 2026-10-30; STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1 since 2026-11-09 11:39) + upstream's STRATA_ADAPT_FETCH commit and the owner's patch that runs it beside the helper GPU, served since 2026-11-09 20:06 with STRATA_ADAPT_FETCH=2. What the fetch patch does: when the main GPU has to read a missed expert from RAM over PCIe and that expert is routed clearly more often than the least-used expert in that layer of the main GPU's cache, the engine keeps the copy in that cache slot instead of dropping it after the window.
engine_notes: The patch series carries, among others: exact speculative sampling (STRATA_SPEC_EXACT), the cost-aware draft gate and cumulative draft length, the fork hyper-connection read (STRATA_GR_FORK), Basalt-derived v2 prompt-expert kernels made bit-identical to the stock path (STRATA_PREFILL_V2), the router's Q8_K doorbell rows (STRATA_ROUTER_Q8K), a chat cache that parks conversations in RAM, and upstream 0.2.7's new defaults pinned off [[src:configs/P028x.json:58]].

The fetch build (`v0.2.8 + 31` in SOURCE) is P028x's 28 commits plus three: upstream's STRATA_ADAPT_FETCH commit (24c6c2f68, from v0.2.12, which turns the switch off when a helper GPU is present); the owner's patch f381bfdf5 that runs it beside the helper (the PCIe share's pick list leaves out experts the helper holds, admissions go to the main GPU's cache only, per-request admission counters and an optional read-back check in serve mode) [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:12-14]] [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:37-58]]; and one commit to the Python server only (an HTTP 400 for a request that names a model which is not loaded), not in the engine binary [[src:strata-r22p028x/serve/server.py:7341]].

With the switch unset the fetch build is bitwise P028x: exact7 7/7 at matched slots, 0 of 40 long-prompt first-token logit files differ [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/decision.txt:3]]. With =2 the GPU computes a different set of experts than P028x would, which changes outputs at rounding level [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:53-57]]; a served-mode sampled-distribution test (D2 1.83 against a noise bound of 11.35) and a read-back of the 91,345 slots admitted in a check run (0 differ) passed [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/decision.txt:14-16]]. exact7 runs without adaptation, where the switch does not act [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:102-103]]; it gave 7/7 with =2 set as well [[src:results/r23/afetch-adopt/summary.txt:55]].
The engine reports `engine 0.1.54` as its session version even though the tree is v0.2.8 + 31; the SOURCE file names the branch commit.

The served config file keeps the name P028x.json, and its own comment line still describes the build before the fetch patch [[src:configs/P028x.json:58]]; its `exe` names the fetch build [[src:configs/P028x.json:2]].

speed_extra_notes: Two workloads (W1-think, R1-verify20k) are two engine requests each: the server ends the thinking pass at its room limit and continues the answer in a second request that reuses the first's state (the second reads only 19 new tokens) [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/speed/F21n.englog:3-10]]. The numbers above count the whole reply, and the server adds the continuation's ~80 ms prompt read to the prompt time, so R1-verify20k's prompt rate reads ~1.5 % low (pass 1: 4,534.5 tok/s for the reply vs 4,601.8 for its first engine request) [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/speed/F21r.englog:2-9]] [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/speed/F21r.jsonl:1]]; W1-think's 111-token prompt rate means nothing for the same reason.
The struct fixture (T 0.0, repetitive structured text) accepts ~96 % of drafts, so its ~237 tok/s is the upper end; W1 / W2 at T 1.0 with thinking are the realistic short-context decode.

Noise, as the spread of the 3 passes per arm in the ADAPT_FETCH gap: screen decode geomean 3.4 %, conv 11.0 %, struct 2.3 %, prose 4.0 % [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/decision.txt:13]]; pp16k / pp64k 0.1 / 0.5 % over 3 passes on the P028x engine before the fetch patch [[src:results/r23/basalt-prompt/gap-speed/decision.txt:9]]. placement_notes: Decode only. The prompt pass works differently: it borrows 3,231 of the main GPU's cache slots for its chunks (section 7), and chunks under 1,792 tokens send 40 % of the expert work to the CPU.

What the fetch patch changes: with STRATA_ADAPT_FETCH=2 a missed expert that the main GPU read over PCIe is kept in the main cache when it is routed clearly more often than the layer's least-used resident expert [[src:results/r23/afetch-adopt/englog/r23aa11091954-S2-decode.englog:47]], about 83 admissions per verify window on the screen. Against the same screen on the P028x engine before the fetch patch, the main cache's share of routed entries rose from 62.6 to 67.3 % and the CPU's fell from 14.4 to 9.4 %; the helper's (17.3 %) and the PCIe share (about 6 %) stayed [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/fetchstats.txt:5]] [[src:results/r23/adaptfetch/gap/fetchstats.txt:9]].

Admissions land only in the main (RTX 5080) cache. The helper's experts are static (filled at start), and the owner's patch makes the PCIe share's pick list leave out experts the helper holds; without that, the picks would go to the helper and never be fetched [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:21-30]] [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:53-55]].

The served log on the current build is short (the 11-09 evening and the 11-10 morning), and four long generations (71,579, 27,946, 32,768 and 15,110 tokens) carry most of its routed entries [[src:logs/engine-P028x.log:238315]] [[src:logs/engine-P028x.log:238519]] [[src:logs/engine-P028x.log:238527]] [[src:logs/engine-P028x.log:238576]]; read the screen as the main figure.

On the P028x engine before the fetch patch (ten days of served traffic, 10-30 to 11-09): about 63 % of routed entries hit the main GPU's cache, 17 % the helper's, 6 % came over PCIe and 14 % were computed by the CPU, and the adaptive tier ran at its cap of 24 swaps per window in every request [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:84]].

memory_notes: The owner's guard stops a run if the main GPU's free memory falls under 300 MiB or MemAvailable under 12 GiB [[src:bringup/lib/guard.py:7-8]] [[src:notes/memavailable-floor.md:8]]; every run above ended `ok`.

Swap in use stayed flat inside every measured run: about 4.3 GiB of other programs' pages were swapped out before the runs began and none moved during them, and the served engine restarted with no swap-out after the gap and after the adoption check (quoted above). The owner's swap rule fails a run on the engine's own swap or on sustained swap traffic inside it, not on pages swapped before it [[src:notes/kernel-oops-pinned-memory.md:51]].
The served config adds the CPU picture reader (about 1 GB of RAM in its own process), not in these runs [[src:notes/memavailable-floor.md:29-30]].

VRAM use is flat by design: the main GPU's expert cache takes all but the reserve at start, so its free memory is the reserve's remainder (about 440-500 MiB) whatever the context; the KV cells past 32,768 per attention layer live in 1.55 GiB of pinned RAM allocated at start, so a 64K prompt costs prompt time and a little RSS (51.5 vs 51.2 GiB for 16K), not VRAM. The fetch patch adds about 260 bytes of VRAM, carved after the cache is sized, so the main cache keeps its 4,585 slots [[src:results/r23/ADAPTFETCH-DESK-1109.md:58]].

notes: **Everything in this section was measured on 11-05 on the P028x engine before the fetch patch, without U.** The fetch patch acts on exactly this split: on the 11-09 screen it cut the CPU's share of routed entries from 14.4 to 9.4 % (section 5), so on the current build the CPU pool takes a smaller part of each window than shown here; whether it is still the slowest step was not measured.

Method: one 9-workload screen pass with STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1 (the host's split per window) and STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 (the GPU stage table); the profile changes the graph (shared expert inline, fused waits off), so its rates run ~2 % low [[src:results/r23/decode-timing/ANALYSIS.md:174-176]]. The first request (warm-up) is left out; means are window-weighted.

Reading it: a window is a serial chain per layer. The GPU runs the dense part of a layer (GDN mixer, hyper-connection reads, router) while the CPU pool idles; then the CPU pool computes the layer's missed experts while the GPU mostly waits (`waitB` in the stage table) [[src:results/r23/decode-timing/ANALYSIS.md:11-14]]. The GPU's serial part is 98-99 % busy with 1.5-3 us of launch gaps per layer, so only kernel work shortens it [[src:results/r23/decode-timing/ANALYSIS.md:15-17]].

The CPU pool (9.67 ms) and the GPU-reach wait (9.60 ms) are nearly equal; per layer-window the CPU pool is the long pole in 69 % of layer-windows on two cards (an older build's trace, 10-21) [[src:results/r23/decode-timing/ANALYSIS.md:89-90]]. Fewer CPU-computed experts (a bigger or smarter GPU cache) is the lever; a faster GPU kernel helps only the other half. The fetch patch is such a lever (section 5).
